text:
Max Sasson keeps scoring on a Vancouver team that keeps losing. He has 6 goals in 20 games, including a redirect against Edmonton on Nov 7, on about 12 and a half minutes a night.

Two things are going on, and they point in opposite directions. His own finishing is running hot: 6 goals on 2.7 expected, a 25% shooting rate that rarely lasts. But with him on the ice, the Canucks have scored 10.8 fewer goals than their chances deserved, which has cost him assists (he has one). That swings back too. The process in between is good: at five on five Vancouver has 48.6% of the expected goals with him out there, 10.7 points better than without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking likes his style: he carried the puck in on 57% of his entries last season, and he gets shots off passes across the slot or from behind the net. An undrafted player out of Western Michigan, he is doing enough to earn more than fourth-line minutes.
headline: Max Sasson is finishing, his linemates are not
